reviews.text: A new non-phone first Metal Slug game since Metal Slug 7 over 16 years ago (which is insane to think about with how many indie run and gun games have come out since then), Metal Slug Tactics from my experience so far is a somewhat faithful modern/slick spinoff of a very beloved oldschool series. Developed by Leiker Studio a French based studio in Paris, the English translation sadly is very lacking at times, with words and sentence structure almost seemingly being nonsensical. Did they have no English speakers to double check this game?? Though this is a series not renowned or even known for it's writing but rather it's action and pixel art, for the most part the artwork holds up very well, the nebulous floating in the void bastion look being just fine, the pixel art also looking as though SNK themselves worked on this title which is pretty impressive, though the blood and gore has been toned down if entirely nurtured, with almost laughable "bouncing" idle animations that do take me out of the experience and don't feel true to Metal Slug. The "soul" of artwork also tends to suffer from being abit too "weeby" with characters being too masculine or sexualized, with way too huge bust size, or everyone always being too overly polite. There is also a very terrible lack of scanline and filtering options when such newer titles like UFO 50 of course didn't forget to include. Also no support for local or online multiplayer is pretty sad to see. :^( Only one game mode and difficulty selection? 😟 I mean hopefully whatever remains of SNK will take notice of this and maybe Metal Slug 8 will finally see the light of day! Would recommend this to tactics fans as those mechanics do have depth and decent variety to them, though if you're a run and gun Metal Slug fan I would probably recommend watching a lets play or staying away from this title. (In terms of art I mean just compared side by side, there are even pervy reviews and comments in the discussions praising this sort of stuff. Again I and many people grew up with Metal Slug in arcades as a kid. I loved it for the goofy wackiness, the master class pixel art, the coop, the frantic energetic gameplay, not because women were being sexualized which is in nearly every piece of Japanese media, and of which in the arcade games was not so in your face and toned down. Marco and Tarma are more skinny, Eri and Fio are more girly and just have fun personalities not based on their giant boobs or the amount of skin they're showing. Look at the character select from the first game, it just ooze's uniqueness and personality for the four main characters. Every single Japanese game now adays is sexualized, it's getting old. Plenty of porn games for you perverts to go play please stay away from Metal Slug.)

Really, Leikir? Could the text be any smaller? If you're a human and not an eagle and feel like you don't have enough eyestrain in your life, play this game. I'm playing on an OLED Deck which has a 7.4 inch screen where the text, the tooltips in particular, are laughably small. It's a bit better on the Legion Go's 8.8-inch screen but that thing's the chonkiest of chonky handhelds. I feel bad for anyone trying to play this on a Switch Lite. I could play on PC instead, but honestly, this game is a perfect fit for handhelds and that's how I want to play it and I imagine many others do too. Leikir, PLEASE, give an option for increasing text size. And playtest your game across some handhelds next time. I'm honestly surprised this wasn't addressed after it was brought up when the playable demo released earlier this year. I'll change my review if this issue is fixed because aside from tiny text, I'm loving everything else about the game.

[h1]《合金弹头》：爷的青春回来了[/h1] 《合金弹头》这款游戏应该是不少人的童年回忆了，也是我的游戏启蒙之一，在当时那个条件并不发达的年代，想要玩游戏就只能去街机厅，而《合金弹头》无疑是街机时代最耀眼的那颗明星，不仅销量长虹、各大游戏厅都能看到他的身影，其在横版过关上的一些经典设计也启发了后来的不少作品。至于其到底有多经典呢？只能说我玩合金弹头的时候都已经是08年、09年了，SKN都已经破产了，但是只要开街机厅的地方就必定有合金弹头——有时候，盗版的传播力度也是一种美。 但无论其过去如何辉煌，也基本都是远古时代的事情了，这个系列的上一部正作《合金弹头》停留在2009年，迄今为止已经过去了15年，没有发布任何正作相关。而实际上《合金弹头XX》也只是《合金弹头7》的威力加强版，因此致力于「经典游戏重置」的Dotemu联系了IP持有者SKN，最终捣鼓出了这么一部《合金弹头：战略版》。 不过相比起前几代正作重置是由SKN授权、Dotemu完成移植工作，本次的《合金弹头：战略版》则是由“小迷弟”Leikir Studio负责开发、Dotemu只是担纲发行，而听到后面「战略版」的tag，你也知道这并不是当初那个经典的合金弹头，而是加入了当今流行的肉鸽跟战棋（好像混进来个奇怪的东西）等元素，一起炖出来一锅还算可口的大杂烩。 [h2]童年的记忆涌上心头[/h2] 首先这款游戏就算在玩法上有所创新，但其底子里还是绕不过《合金弹头》这个IP。从进入游戏大厅界面开始，虽然不是那个熟悉的子弹风选人，但是人物建模、表情以及一些场景细节等等都还是童年味道满满，角色也是合金弹头里面的经典人物。 在肉鸽部分开始以后，对大地图的选择就更加是“融入经典“了，不仅能看到许多以前的经典地图，敌人设计也与原版保持一致，那些抖动的像素细节真是让人有几分梦回当年的感觉，总而言之，这款游戏在视觉效果上一定不会让你失望，唯一可能就是立绘比较现代化一点，或许会让部分粉丝感到不适应，谁让咱们接触的都是合金弹头靠前的几部作品呢！ [h2]肉鸽+战棋，究竟该怎么做？[/h2] 游戏的玩法并不是传统的卷轴射击，这也许会让一些粉丝失望了，终究是不能看到这个IP再度散发自己的魅力。但我觉得可能是SKN不让授权搞这个：要是你自己出了个横版续作，那我之后想要搞情怀牌的话先消耗了信誉值又找谁说理去？所以只能搞一些跟原版玩法不同的衍生作品。 不过在人物的战斗表现上还是以射击为主，只是配合上了战棋的玩法（什么X-COM），再配合上新式肉鸽的框架，这样一部肉鸽战棋就烹饪完成了。其实肉鸽战棋在近些年也不算什么新鲜类型，毕竟今年已经是《陷阵之志》这样的传奇作品诞生的第六个年头了，早早就为行业树立了标杆，后来者们基本上照抄完事，市面上也有其他不少优秀作品。 而《合金弹头：战略版》给人的观感，大概就是Leikir Studio只有厨力、不适合做战棋。但我也不是一名资深战棋玩家，所以给不出啥有力见解，只是觉得它们或许可以让玩家更爽一点。目前的爽点主要是来自于「连携」，也就是玩家与队友移动到同一范围内，会触发合力攻击，再加上本作有「移动减伤」机制，距离越远就越容易闪避，所以传统战棋里的「移动」在本作中就更加重要，简单讲操作逻辑就是「打一枪换一炮」。再加上肉鸽部分在本作中占比并不突出，而战棋的味道则要浓郁，所以说白了是没有吸收到《陷阵之志》的优点，还是比较靠近传统战棋——这也是目前评论区差评的主要来源：内容太少。 [h2]总结[/h2] 总的来说，我觉得游戏素质还是不错的，作为一款战棋其设计还是相对古朴，但也是充满了满满的策略性，无论是移动还是连携都有比较多的思考量。可惜与此同时也牺牲了一点爽度，对于那些想要在“肉鸽战棋”里感受头脑风暴的玩家来说，太过被规矩限制有时候也像是在寸止挑战。还是希望能在目前的基础上，尽可能往游戏里加入更多内容吧。 [quote] 执笔勾墨色，挥毫著文章；阳春布德泽，璞玉生光辉 欢迎关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44174077/]吟遊诗人的手札[/url]，书游戏特色，写游戏魅力 [/quote]

Metal Slug Tactics is an interesting one. It's got a very unique attack system that places an emphasis on constant movement and synchronising attacks between your characters. Movement gives you dodge, which is a form of armor; and adrenaline, which is the equivalent of mana. Therefore, a turn not utilising movement range can really work against you. While many other turn-based games out there involves 10-20 turns, most missions in MS Tactics can and ideally should be completed in 1-5 turns due to the fact that the odds are [b]always[/b] against you. It's pretty funny how with the ideal builds, I can often complete missions before the enemy even has a chance to get a turn. This game is definitely a lot harder than the others in the genre, because you HAVE to make optimal moves and actions every turn in order to succeed. And because of how different MST is to other games, it might take a number of missions before you understand which special actions and weapon mods to take. This is without question more challenging than Advance Wars or Final Fantasy Tactics. And while I really like the original take on the turn-based tactics genre, I do feel like the roguelite aspect of the game kinda ruins the fun a bit. On harder difficulties, you probably will want to restart runs if you don't unlock the abilities you need early on. Because scaling isn't done very well, completing early missions can be extremely tedious due to your limited access to abilities. Overall, Metal Gear Tactics should be a no-brainer for anyone who's a fan of tactical turn-based games. I do hope we get a proper turn-based tactics game with progression and team compositions one day. Lord knows there's no shortage of Metal Slug characters.

Good game for the first 20 hours or so. But gradually, the freshness runs out and you start to see the frustrating side of the game. 1. Bugs and endless bugs Now in my save i've unlocked every upgrade, BUT the game thinks there's 24 grenade upgrade when there's only 23, and keeps reminding me to go there and get the last NONE-EXISTING upgrade. Like every time you go to the lobby, there's a giant exclamation mark that forces you to look at the bug, truly brilliant design. Saving a game mid-battle for dinner, and come back later, load the battle -- guess what, the map intractable are gone, disarmed traps were active again. And there's more to it, sometimes you load the game, and found there's no one in the map. Only to find ALL CHARACTERS including enemies are stuck in a SINGLE TILE by the corner of the map. Finished a difficult unlock but the game doesn't recognize it (throwing an enemy with Clark, and let sticky bomb explode on a mind-controlled enemy). If you want to make unlocks so specific and niche, please make sure the game could properly detect it. 2. Repeated and Untested stages. Firstly, there's only so few mission types/maps, and the game kinda encourages you to play through 4/4 areas every run (for true ending you'd have to). Resulting in a heavy amount of repeated experience. Honestly, i'd like a game better if it's 3 areas rotating out of 5, which extends the life-time and freshness a lot. Other other hand, it has very poorly tested stages, especially escort. It seems like they didn't test the jungle escorts at all. You got a VIP to protect and every single turn, the VIP will move to an exposed tile within 3-5 enemy's attack range. Plus the jungle maps are filled with multiply height levels, so some enemies are just none-approachable/not worth to approach. You might need to meat shield VIP a couple times but even that is bad, since being a meat-shield and not killing enemy results in more enemies to kill next turn. On the other hand, you got mini-boss with 30 hp, that got downed in a single turn. Yes, the difficulty is THAT random. 3. Very inconsistent character skills You get special skills that allows you to kill 20 enemy in one turn (special action kill returns action point), that just carries the game. Or skill combos that stacks damage easily (dodge talents + burst). And on the other hand, you get skills that gives +1 to mind-controlled enemy, which you have no control over. I mean....i like randomness but this is a bit on the cheap side really, the game is to the point when you see a certain pick-up, you know how the rest of it plays. The pool is made not deep enough and poorly combined for repeated runs. Conclusion: Like i said, if you plan to just play for 20 hours than it's quite potentially a good pick. But the problem is that, the developers seems to have made a blurred decision on the life-span of the game. On one side, they seem to want to extend the game's life by lots of very specific achievements(and you need them to fully unlock character/see their ending), and rather slow unlocks that's tied to achievements. However, on the other side, they seem to expect the game to be a lite/short-life experience, looking at very small pools of upgrade/maps. With addition of all those bugs (which is still not fully fixed until today), i can't give a recommendation so far. If they fix ALL the weird bugs, i'd recommend the game for a short-period fun (around 20-40 hours).

Although I only played for two hours before deciding it was not for me, I can still reccomend this pending on your preferences. This is a turn based tile strategy, similar to Into The Breach. If you liked it, you will enjoy this. For me, this felt a lot more of a tactical strategy and positioning game, rather than more combos with mix and matching archetypes that I like. The game heavily revolves around sync-shots (every character shoots enemies if in line of sight when an ally strikes an enemy), and run-gun tactics making it quite strategical in planning out your moves. It is very similar to Into The Breach, where progression only unlocks different base weapons and loadouts, with only 3 playable characters in any party. I prefer more roguelike-types with some sort of progression where your character(s) get stronger over time to tackle increasing difficulty, rather than tackling increased difficulty with stronger mastery of your characters. 6/10.

Well, I finally got around to playing a spin-off of one of my favorite franchises only to find it’s a roguelite after 1.5 hours of play. Got killed by a boss and had to start the game over again from scratch!? No thanks. I have limited time to game as an adult with a career and family and no interest in “beating” a game multiple times in escalating difficulty settings to get the actual ending. Why does this genre even exist? If Xcom can make a traditional campaign that combines perma-death WITH seeing everything the game has to offer in a single campaign, then what’s the excuse for this game? Laziness. Instead of create a campaigns worth of thrilling levels, bosses, and character development they force you to fight in the same battles, over and over again with different difficult settings. How lazy is that!? Hard pass. And that sucks because the world, art design, and music are all great. If they update it with a traditional campaign structure I’ll update my review.

The tactics gameplay is pretty fun and the pixel art is fantastic. However, it's a roguelite and I do not see why it needs to be. I don't think the game justified why it was a roguelite because it doesn't really do anything interesting with the mechanic. The roguelite elements feel tacked on and there is a severe lack of variety with missions. I failed a run once and it was frustrating having to redo everything when basically nothing changed on my next run. On my second attempt, I completed the run but there was a lot I didn't do because I just went straight for the final boss. I don't really feel compelled to do another run at this point. Also, certain story segments are locked behind a grind which is unfortunate. The main story in the game is virtually nonexistent and you don't really build any type of bond with the characters. This game is purely gameplay first, but the gameplay isn't anything to write home about. I would have preferred a linear tactics game that was more focused and tailored. I did have some fun playing the game, but if you're looking for a good tactics/strategy game, there are much better options out there. I wouldn't recommend buying it unless there is a sale. 6/10 for me.

Wish I could recommend this, because it nailed the metal slug vibe in some ways. The problem is basically that this is a game where the bones are good, but then there isn't much content to make use of them. -Alternate loadouts and mods are very low impact and boring -Every run is very samey. I know people say this about roguelikes a lot, but this one is the worst i've played in that regard. There are only 4 areas, and after your first run you'll have seen every enemy, mission, and boss in the entire game. There aren't any alternate routes, It's the same 2-3 mission types, and upgrades dont add anything to how you play really. -Kills don't feel satisfying, because boss fights and most stages just kind of dump endless enemies on you. If it's not a "kill them all" mission, then all you want to do is make a beeline to the objective/kill you need because everything else just wastes your time. -Doesn't feel super tactical, since the game pretty much gives you shields for running max distance all the time. I get the "run n gun" idea, but in practice it feels kind of dumb to play around the weird hit patterns most weapons have, cover, momentum, and synch. Basically, this was potential for a great game that fell flat in execution and was low on content. Its not a bad game. I had fun for like 2 playthroughs, but then the thought of any more was an absolute nope. Same 4 biomes, same four bosses, just not enough variety. Its a game that screams for more content via dlc or modding. They didn't even give us an alien stage. It's metal slug!

Metal Slug tactics is a Nintendo Switch game that was ported (badly) to PC as an attempt from SNK to wring blood out of a stone and abuse the Metal Slug franchise for every penny they can squeeze out of it. It's getting worse than the bit in Spaceballs when they showed off all the merchandise like "Spaceballs: The Toilet Paper". This time they decided to see if PC gamers would tolerate a Nintendo Switch turn based tactical game if they didn't bother testing it properly (it's full of bugs) and did a mediocre effort porting it to PC. And even for a Nintendo Switch "roguelike", this is a shallow and pointless wreck of a game. On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met. Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers. Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies. Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for. These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers. The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game. While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC. To make matters worse, not only does this have pixelcrap "art", the pixelcrap isn't even applied consistently across the whole game. That jarring mismatch ruins any genuine "retro" authenticity from this pixelcrap nightmare. The inconsistency with the pixelcrap is a tacit admission that the developer was aware they could have done better but chose not to. Making a game look bad, on purpose. That's an insult. While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality. Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals. The game features no proper level design or game/story flow/plot, as they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen algorithms as a substitute for adding such content to the game, to avoid doing the important job of level/map design. As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning, just endless, boring, repetitive, soulless algorithmically generated sameyness. Developers must learn that procedural generation is not an acceptable substitute for content. We know Roguelites and Roguelikes are mostly slapped together by developers who are basically lazy and don't want to create bespoke content, resulting in that shallow, repetitive, soulless experience of procgen algorithms instead of content, but this is even shallower than most, there's just a couple of map forms and a couple of randomly placed enemy types, so you've seen the entire game after the first couple of missions. Worse, you have to grind those samey missions to unlock more of the "game", such as it is. This is painful, especially considering the woeful visuals and technical quality. These technical shortcomings push this game below minimum standards for any competently developed modern PC game. You're forced to sign a highly questionable yet legally unenforceable End User License Agreement... for such a relatively low effort, low quality game this comes across more as a delusion of grandeur than anything else. This agreement includes questionable requirements that may attempt to revoke consumer law protections that gamers expect to have, which is also highly problematic. Developers must learn they are here to serve gamers, not control them. I had my cat walk over the keyboard while the EULA was displaying, which fixed that problem for me. Now on to pricing and value for gamers. So, should you buy this game? Is this one of the best of the 140,000+ games on Steam? Metal Slug Tactics has the preposterous price of $25 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games. For comparison, the INSANE $25 asking price for this game could get you games like "Crusader Kings III", "Mount and Blade 2 Bannerlord" or "Rimworld". Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this. Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend. No pixelcrap is worth $25. If developers want to get paid the same kind of money as real game developers who know how to do graphics properly, they need to learn how to do graphics properly.

Metal Slug Tactics was a pleasant surprise. It successfully brings the classic Metal Slug charm into a turn-based tactical format while keeping the series' iconic style and personality. The pixel art is gorgeous, the animations are fantastic, and the soundtrack perfectly complements the action. The gameplay encourages constant movement, making battles feel dynamic and rewarding. Learning how to combine different characters and abilities adds a lot of depth, and every run feels fresh thanks to the roguelite elements and progression system. Whether you're a long-time Metal Slug fan or simply enjoy tactical games, this one is definitely worth checking out. It's stylish, challenging, and incredibly fun, with plenty of replay value. A great tribute to the classic series and an easy recommendation from me.

[h1]𝕄𝕀𝕊𝕊𝕀𝕆ℕ... 𝕊𝕋𝔸ℝ𝕋![/h1] For decades, the Metal Slug series has been synonymous with frantic run-and-gun action, explosive set pieces, and beautifully animated pixel art. Metal Slug Tactics takes that familiar formula and reimagines it as a turn-based tactical game --a risky move that surprisingly pays off. Metal Slug Tactics is still, somehow, its own game. It doesn't copy mechanics of other strategy titles but it keeps the basics. Battles are all about aggressive play, rewarding movement and positioning instead of passive defense. Characters can snowball through the battlefield through their unique stats, passives and active abilities and fans of the franchise will LOVE to play as their favourite characters, such as Marco, Fio, Eri, Trevor and even characters from the Ikari Warrior team, so basically King of Fighters (Clark, Ralf, Leona). You unlock more of the game as you unlock more achievements. Yes, most of the game, then, rewards you with more of it as you show adaptation and evolution in the battlefield. The transition to tactical format could've stipped away the series' personality, but the devs here clearly understood what makes Metal Slug, well, Metal Slug... It's the unique pixel art that features exceptional movement, fluid animations and expressive character designs that rival even the most classic entries in the genre. Another welcome addition is the roguelite structure. Some, of course, will find the four recurrent regions in the game boring and repetitive at some point, I found it adds a layer of "trial and error" to the game, as no single run will be exactly as the next and these characters all have different loadouts and different strategies they use. An example of this would be Fio, which you can build as a machinegun powerhouse, OR as a buffing support for your team, who can reposition her allies and buff them with defense and dodge, the same way Tarma can be one of the bulkiest tanks on the battlefield, or a simple medic. However, the game is not that perfect, as the random nature of some runs can occasionally lead to uneven difficulty spikes, where one level is a breeze and the next is total torture. The soundtrack, though, helps wrestle through it, it's amazing, catchy, and I've finished the game, like fully, and it's still stuck in my head and I can't get it out of my head. Despite these concerns, Metal Slug Tactics succeeds where many genre transformations have failed. It respects source material while confidently exploring new territories. the result is a tactical strategy game that feels unmistakably Metal Slug-est; fast, explosive, humorous and endlessly charming. [b]9.5/10[/b]

I won this game through SteamGifts. I'll admit when I won this game, I wasn't convinced I'd enjoy it. Turns out I was pleasantly surprised! The pixel art is fantastic, the animations are full of personality, and the tactical gameplay is genuinely fun. It does a great job of translating the classic Metal Slug feel into a turn-based roguelite. My biggest issue is that the roguelite side of things starts to feel a bit repetitive after a while. There just isn't enough variety in enemies, and the pool of upgrades and abilities feels a little too limited, especially considering how often you'll see the same options pop up during a run. I kept wishing there was a bit more to shake things up. The achievement list also felt a bit bloated. I usually enjoy going for 100%, but this time I just wasn't interested because so many of them felt unnecessary rather than rewarding. Overall though, I had a much better time than I expected. It may not have enough variety to keep me playing forever, but it's a fun tactical spin on the Metal Slug formula that's definitely worth checking out if you're a fan of the series or roguelites.

Ok, i bought this game on release and played plenty so i can give a review, i actually held on for a time, because i thought the devs would at least fix some of my worries, but enough time has passed and they never fixed anything so here it goes: the game itself its not bad at all, you quickly understand what its trying to do and how it plays, you suddenly become good enough to exploit the strenght of the characters and up the difficulty. but all of this is ruined by one thing, BUGS, there have been so many runs that ended in a soft-lock because the programmers didnt do their work correctly, a bad turn, a bad re-start, or just the use of some skills in certain ways can make the game soft-locked and you cant continue because either the enemies get stuck, or your characters get stuck, or the menus get stuck, or the maps simply wont continue the next turn, and its such a waste of time because each run is like 1 hour, this has even happened to me on the final boss fight, so imagine that, surviving 3 boss fights and end up getting soft-locked during the final of the final. if it wasnt for this, i would recommend it, but as it is, and knowing that the devs seemingly abandoned it, then i wont recommend.

这游戏有一个大问题和若干个小问题，剩下的就都是优点了。 大问题在于：战棋受众天然和合金弹头的IP互斥。如果你是合金弹头粉丝，那我劝你别买；如果你是陷阵之志粉丝，那我劝你赶紧入手。 小问题在于：BUG实在有点多，虽然已经修复过好几轮了，但依然有很多残留。文字显示/描述BUG就有五六处，另外还有BUFF结算和伤害计算BUG（只发生在被动技能特别多的情况下） 优点在于：1.精美像素风，以及非常多的原作要素；2.组合多，总共9个人物×4个模组，不同的排列组合能产生很多意料之外的化学反应，且人物之间的区分度极大；3.上限高，很容易达成一回合清屏或者秒BOSS的操作，作为肉鸽游戏能不能让玩家爽是一个很重要的因素；4.存在兜底机制，不管是技能的重ROLL还是免费的悔棋都极高的提升了游戏体验，比那些动不动就让人重开的游戏好太多了。 最后还有个不知道算优点还是缺点的地方：这游戏非常杀时间。

——记录：《合金弹头：战略版》，January 2026 Humble Choice月包，2026/01/07入。 ——合金弹头系列首款回合制战术衍生作，将经典街机跑轰爽感融入战棋框架，用「移动 = 防御 + 技能资源」的创新机制跳出了传统战棋蹲坑对射的固有模式，情怀还原到位，玩法辨识度十足。受限于轻度肉鸽设计与内容体量，多周目重复感偏高，属于系列粉丝必玩、战棋爱好者可酌情入手的情怀向佳作。 ——综合评分：7.5/10 ——背景&剧情：故事延续系列经典设定：反乱军首领唐纳德・摩登将军卷土重来，在敌对国家蛰伏多年后积蓄兵力发动政变，妄图向世界政府复仇。玩家将率领游隼隼小队深入战区，一路突破敌军防线，逐个击破区域 BOSS 据点，最终挫败摩登的战争阴谋。 ——核心创新：移动 = 闪避 + 肾上腺素。 这是本作最具辨识度的机制，从根本上改变了战棋的防守逻辑：角色每回合移动距离越远，获得的闪避值越高，闪避相当于临时护盾，可直接抵消伤害，掩体的减伤效果反而十分有限；长距离移动同时会积攒肾上腺素，相当于技能能量，用于释放手雷、冲刺射击、范围轰炸等特殊招式；所有攻击必定命中，没有miss概率，不用赌脸，所有伤害与生存收益都和走位直接挂钩，鼓励玩家全程拉扯、主动出击，完美复刻了原作边跑边打的爽感。 ——是一次非常成功的系列玩法跨界尝试，它没有生硬地把合金弹头套进战棋模板，而是抓住了「跑轰」的核心气质，用创新机制让两种玩法完美契合。对于系列老粉丝来说，光是满屏的情怀细节就值回票价；对于纯战棋玩家来说，它的机制有新意但深度稍欠，更适合中等体量的休闲体验。 ——适合合金弹头系列粉丝、喜欢快节奏战术游戏、偏爱创新机制战棋、追求像素复古情怀的玩家。26/07/21
